body:
Parent: #22 (Evidence & Data Trust).

## Traceability and dependencies
Requirements: FR-01–FR-07; SC-01–SC-04 (defined in parent epic breakdown).
Depends on: #36, #37, #38

## Outcome
The epic's acceptance criteria are demonstrated by a small reproducible example and meaningful regression checks, with clear operating limits.

## Scope and technical plan
- Add an offline end-to-end example: fixture extraction → normalization → supplier/manufacturer conflict resolution → SQLite restart/retrieval → portable export/load → inspectable trust report.
- Include missing price/stock/currency, explicit zero/false, nested variants, transformed identifiers, conflicting values, unsupported LLM output and expired evidence.
- Map every spec requirement and epic acceptance criterion to a named test/example in `tasks.md`; perform the Spec Kit consistency review and record remaining limitations.
- Document public APIs, source precedence, retention, export compatibility, migration and model-score versus validated-confidence semantics in README/docs.
- Verify affected extraction, identity/comparison, snapshot/monitoring and export compatibility. No broad live crawl or local inference sweep is necessary.

## Acceptance scenarios and success criteria
- SC-01: 100% of factual fields in the bounded fixture coverage matrix have retrievable evidence or explicit unsupported/unknown/expired states.
- SC-02: Every conflict fixture retains competing observations and a selected-value explanation or unresolved reason.
- SC-03: Supported IDs/source data/field states/resolutions survive restart and lossless export/load without semantic changes.
- SC-04: Legacy fixture behavior and affected regression suites pass; calibration claims are absent unless backed by named validation artifacts.
- A fresh user can run the documented offline example and retrieve evidence without hosted services or paid feature gates.

## Completion gate
Close the epic only when the linked child criteria and actual verification are complete; planning or a successful demo alone is insufficient. Save a compact verification summary with commands, outcomes and limitations.

## Spec Kit workflow
Use one shared feature directory, `specs/002-evidence-data-trust/`. Specify user outcomes and Given/When/Then scenarios in `spec.md`; record architecture, compatibility and resolved questions in `plan.md`; maintain dependency-ordered, requirement-linked work in `tasks.md`. Update the relevant artifacts before implementation and verify spec/plan/tasks consistency before closing this ticket. These are required implementation deliverables, not artifacts already generated by an installed Spec Kit workflow.

## Boundaries and definition of done
Evidence-backed reporting only; no catalog mutations, MCP, webhooks, or other epic work. Preserve MIT licensing and self-hostability. Prefer deterministic, offline fixtures; no model launch or broad live crawl is required. Document public APIs and limitations, and run meaningful affected compatibility checks. Do not equate extraction quality, rule/model scores, and validated confidence.
title: [Epic 2] Demonstrate evidence trust end to end and document compatibility
